title: Chromium Breaks the Rule? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Copper wires, a shiny chrome tap and an iron pan: three metals almost side by side in the periodic table, and two of them break a rule. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we write electronic configurations and find out why chromium and copper are special.

You will see the s p d f notation and the orbital diagram for sodium, then build atoms on the molecule bench one electron at a time from hydrogen to scandium, with 4s filling before 3d and the noble gas core written as [Ar]. Then chromium and copper: the rules predict [Ar] 3d4 4s2 and [Ar] 3d9 4s2, but one 4s electron moves into 3d to give [Ar] 3d5 4s1 and [Ar] 3d10 4s1. We explain why half filled and completely filled subshells are extra stable (symmetry and exchange energy), count the 10 exchanges in 3d5 against 6 in 3d4, work out iron ([Ar] 3d6 4s2, 4 unpaired electrons), and finish with the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 25 of our PUC Chemistry series. Episode 24 covers the Aufbau principle, the Pauli exclusion principle and Hund's rule.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
